title: Inference with Dependent Data in Accounting and Finance
sources_checked: Accepted author package source Datasheet and ReplicationFiles/FRQMainMat.csv: SHA-256 864a9d4572ce19cee64a72b5020aa1297f363b0a7dda4964d30cb5b0ae6d3cd2; aggregate-only scan of the fyear column found 21,290 rows across 17 consecutive years, 1993–2009. This is the direct-provided baseline file, not a refreshed current-vintage panel.

Current local Compustat source COMP.FUNDA at ${ACCTREPL_SAS_ROOT}/comp/d_na/funda.sas7bdat (7,258,374,144 bytes; 941,340 rows; file mtime 2026-07-22 UTC): streamed only fyear and datadate, with fiscal-year labels 1950–2026 and records in 2010–2014. This verifies Compustat fundamentals coverage only.

Local resource catalog output/feasibility_reproduction/resources/catalog.json (generated 2026-10-27): lists COMP.FUNDA and warns that metadata is a discovery snapshot, not verified access, license entitlement, or historical field coverage.

Pinned author simulation inputs FRQSim_FINAL_BOOT.mat, FRQSim_FINAL_FIRMTIME.mat, FRQSim_FINAL_PART2_GAUSS.mat and SizePt1–Pt4_1000X2000_bsize3_17Obs_sim_1000.mat: file hashes match the assigned predecessor records; scipy.io.whosmat header checks only, with no variable values loaded.
changes: Resolved the baseline annual fyear clock from FRQMainMat.csv as 1993–2009 (17 consecutive years), so the assigned five-year endpoint is 2014.

Left the accepted estimator and stage code unchanged. No extended fit was prepared or launched because all assigned stages are simulation post-processors, and the named local inputs contain no refreshed pooled calibration panel or newly generated simulation arrays.
limitations: The author package README identifies FRQMainMat.csv as an already-prepared Balakrishnan et al. panel input (line 5); FRQFitMean.m imports this CSV (line 7), while FRQSim_GenY.m generates synthetic outcomes from existing estimates. The packaged panel ends in 2009. No current refreshed full panel or existing local construction route for the non-Compustat fields was identified among the named inputs.

Although current local COMP.FUNDA has fiscal-year observations through 2014 and later, the paper says the baseline panel was directly provided by Rodrigo Verdi and its variables include reporting quality, real-estate values, and state real-estate indices. Compustat coverage alone does not establish coverage of or reconstruct that 66-column panel.

Inherited gap G_NUMTOLATEX_FORMATTING remains for mbb_power: the original power code calls absent NumToLatex.m for five output-only groups; the accepted predecessor captured the computed arrays and five Vk=1 rows but not that formatting.

The assigned scopes cover the wild-bootstrap summary, firm-year summary, MBB size summaries, and MBB power summary. Other paper results and unexecuted programs remain outside this assignment, including the missing README-listed FRQSim_FinalStats.m and other Table 1, Tables 4–6, and non-MBB Table 7 results.

analyses.label: Cluster wild-bootstrap size summaries (Table 2)
analyses.reason: Not applicable to a temporal sample extension: this assigned stage summarizes a fixed Monte Carlo design and consumes precomputed simulation arrays. The underlying baseline is the exact author-provided panel in FRQMainMat.csv (21,290 firm-years; fyear 1993–2009), while the requested five-year endpoint is 2014. The paper says the simulations condition on the observed regressors and firm/time IDs as a fixed design, and the assigned summary code does not estimate a pooled firm-year model or generate new simulated outcomes. Local COMP.FUNDA covers 2010–2014 fiscal years, but it is only one input source and cannot reconstruct the author-provided calibration panel. No added calendar-year observations enter this branch. This stage computes rejection proportions over 1,000 stored simulation draws; its statistical unit is simulation replication by coefficient, with 17 fixed time IDs in the underlying design.
source_evidence: Paper: papers/parsed/jar-3d876a58201e.json, §4 p.38 and footnote 19: 1,000 simulated datasets condition on observed regressors and firm/time identifiers; the design is fixed. §4.2 p.48 and Table 2 p.68 identify cluster wild-bootstrap size results.
